## 2. Bar kernel: pnf_14 (point-and-figure columns), exact rules
Code: code/th_bars/kernels.py:247-271 `k_pnf`, built at code/th_bars/build_month.py:135-136 (rows 5,7,10,14,20,28,40,56). Integer ticks (0.25 pt), every tape RECORD one step, no print merge (row UNAFFECTED by the D8 print rule, D8_PRINT_RULE.md section 5). Same code and wording as D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md section 3, restated here with box = 14-row:
- Box B (ticks, fixed per trading date): `B = max(1, round(14 * s_rng))`, numpy round half-to-even (build_month.py:136; s_rng from the day-scale table below). td 20261027: 31 ticks = 7.75 pt; td 20261110: 43 ticks = 10.75 pt.
- State resets (no bar emitted, open column dropped) at every change of key (td x 10 + session code) or instrument id (kernels.py:253).
- First column (kernels.py:255-260): the first print of the session sets lvl = st = p, t0 = its time, d = 0. While d = 0: first print with p >= lvl + B starts an UP column (d = 1, st = lvl, lvl = lvl + floor((p-lvl)/B)*B); first print with p <= lvl - B starts a DOWN column (st = lvl, lvl = lvl - floor((lvl-p)/B)*B).
- No fixed grid: every level = the session's first print price +- whole multiples of B (re-anchored at every session start).
- Extension: UP column, p >= lvl + B -> lvl += floor((p-lvl)/B)*B (several boxes at once allowed); DOWN mirrored (lines 262, 267). No bar emitted.
- Reversal, only tested if the print did not extend the column (elif): UP column reverses when p <= lvl - 3*B (exactly 3 boxes counts), DOWN when p >= lvl + 3*B (lines 263, 268).
- Emitted bar (one per COMPLETED column, at the confirming print): UP column o = st, h = lvl, l = st, c = lvl; DOWN column o = st, h = st, l = lvl, c = lvl (lines 264, 269): high/low are grid levels, not the extreme print.
- New column after a reversal: st = lvl - B (up-to-down) or lvl + B (down-to-up), i.e. one box beyond the old extreme; new lvl = old lvl -+ floor(|old lvl - p|/B)*B (>= 3 boxes beyond the old extreme) (lines 265, 270).
- Volume/count/delta accumulate from the column's first print including the confirming print (line 257 before the tests); reset to 0 after the reversal, so the confirming print belongs to the OLD bar. Known time = timestamp of the confirming print (line 264 `ts[i]`). The open column at session end is NOT emitted (no flush; part = 0 always). Bar range (high - low) of a bar = at least 2 boxes.
- VERIFIED: rebuilt from the tape (NY AM td 20261027: 169,694 records, B 31; td 20261110: 234,912 records, B 43): 38 and 83 bars, all of o, h, l, c, vol, n, t0, known, part identical to /mnt/l2/l2vast/_bars/pnf_14.
**Day scales (how the per-day constant is built; identical code for every book of this page).** code/th_bars/build_month.py:13-32 `scales()`: for each trading date (td = ET + 6 h) the stats row of the 20 stats rows BEFORE that td (the current day is never used; values <= 0 dropped; at least 5 values, else the first-60-day median) are medianed; scale = that median / (median of the first 60 days). Columns: `rng` = daily range in points, built per UTC trade file, max over the pieces, / 4 (code/th_bars/stats.py:18; the quirk and the A/B holes are written out in autopilot/D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md section 2); `vol` = contracts of every record of the td; `n` = number of PRINTS of the td (run merge, same price and same tape side, never across a session code), table /mnt/l2/l2vast/_d8spec/runstats/stats_day.parquet. Checked here: for td 20261110 the runstats `n` = 463,946 = my own run count of the store tape (same price + same store side, break at session-code change): equal; the `_bars` stats_day.parquet holds the record count 530,480 instead (different column), so a coder must use the merged-print count for dib / tick rows.
**Data end / holes (read first).** The engine's stats tables end at td 20261113 and have no row for 20261102, 20261103, 20261104 (and 20261105 is a half day; autopilot/D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md header). The engine trade store also lacks the days 20261102-20261104 (trade files present: 1026-1030, 1105, 1106, 1108, 1109, 1110..1113). Column A = the engine as stored (what the stored bars and events used); column B (rng-based constants only) = the same function on a table with the holes filled and 1116-1120 added from hist_replica (a FORMULA result from D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md section 2, not an engine run). Which of A or B NT8 should copy for tomorrow is NOT decided here (lead).

## 3. Trigger: trig_levels_fibr_on, variant false_break (plain), M 3, k 0.5
Code: code/th_grid/triggers_d/lv_fibr_on.py (line list), lv_base.py:23-45, fd_common.py:58 level_events (false_break at :82-87), :20-37 decision time / lookup, :46-57 edge / roll_any, :112-119 events_to_frame; line build code/th_grid/triggers_d/fd_levels.py:30 (ON high/low) and fd_levels2.py:131-137 (`range_fib`).
1. Series: one continuous series of all stored pnf_14 bars (all sessions since 2023-04, sorted by known time); only the signal bar must be NY AM with part = 0.
2. Plain variant: u = 5.0 points FIXED (lv_base.py `U0 = 5.0`), so k x u = 0.5 x 5.0 = 2.5 points (INPUTS columns u_native_pts = 5, k_times_u = 2.5; no native unit, the u in the INPUTS is the constant).
3. Lines (18, raw prices in points; priority = list order): FIBR_ON_DN236, DN382, DN500, DN618, DN650, DN786, UP236, UP382, UP500, UP618, UP650, UP786, XU1272, XU1618, XU2000, XD1272, XD1618, XD2000. Let H, L = highest/lowest price of the OVERNIGHT range = every minute from 18:00 ET (evening before) to 09:29 ET, R = H - L; lines exist only if R >= 8 points and only from 09:30 ET on (fd_levels.py:30 `after(.., 930)`; minute i uses minutes < i). DN_r = H - r R; UP_r = L + r R (r = 0.236, 0.382, 0.5, 0.618, 0.65, 0.786); XU_e = H + (e-1) R; XD_e = L - (e-1) R (e = 1.272, 1.618, 2.0) (fd_levels2.py:131-136). Values stored float32.
4. Level at bar j: line value at the last minute START <= T0_j = previous bar's known time in whole seconds; NaN if that minute is more than 120 s older (fd_common.py:20-37). So bars whose T0 is before 09:30 ET (the first bar of the session if the previous bar closed before 09:30:00) have no level. Example 1110: first bar T0 14:25:30Z -> no lines; second bar T0 14:30:07Z -> lines present.
5. Per line: up_j = close_j > L_j + 2.5; dn_j = close_j < L_j - 2.5 (level-true, each bar with its own L); SHORT mask = (up on any of bars j-3, j-2, j-1) AND close_j < L_j; LONG mask = (dn on any of j-3..j-1) AND close_j > L_j; then edge (kept only if the mask was False on bar j-1). Strict inequalities.
6. OR over the 18 lines; first line (list order) that fires = `fired`; a bar with both long and short is dropped. Failed upside break -> SHORT, failed downside -> LONG (the break is FADED).
VERIFIED: engine module = events file 25,009 / 25,009 (ts, side); my implementation on the INPUTS = 21 / 58; the 18 lines from the tape: ON H/L (td 20261027: H 29628.75, L 29288.00, R 340.75; td 20261110: H 28109.00, L 27590.00, R 519.00) give DN/UP/XU/XD values equal to the table (max diff 0.001).
Data NT8 needs: the overnight high/low only (from 18:00 ET to 09:29 ET, tick or 1-minute high/low).

## 5. Bracket S8U (unit rule spelled out), sides, window, one position
- S8U = symmetric 8 x u (code/th_brkt/brkt_build.py:17): stop = target = clip(8 * u, 10, 120) points (cl at line 15, applied to the unit-rule product; stop and target equal).
- u = rolling MEDIAN over the last 50 bars of (high - low) in POINTS of THIS book's pnf_14 bars, window INCLUDING the signal bar, min_periods 10 (fallback = median of all bar ranges if NaN), floor 0.25 (brkt_build.py:40; same line in code/th_nyeng/ny_build.py:30). The window is the continuous bar series of ALL sessions (not only NY AM). u is evaluated at the signal bar. It is per signal, not per day.
- Units: bar high - low in points; stop/target in points from the entry fill; 1 lot.
- Result in practice: pnf_14 bar range >= 2 boxes; since 2026-04 every event of the file has stop = target = 120.0 (monthly share of events with stop 120: 100% for 202604-202611, n 155-831 per month; file minimum in 2026 = 120). Older history (2023-25, small boxes) had 18.5% of events below 120 (min 72). On the sample days u_bracket_pts >= 31.00 so 8u >> 120. The 8u product reaches 120 only below u = 15 pt; the box today is 31-43 ticks (7.75-10.75 pt) so a bar range is >= 15.5-21.5 pt. A fixed 120/120 therefore reproduces the engine as long as the box stays >= 31 ticks; kept as a rule line, lead may choose fixed 120/120 (NOT decided here).
- Sides: both. Window: NY AM bars (code 3), part 0; session-end exit 12:00 ET + 1 s.
**Signal to engine event (VERIFIED in code).** Event time `ts` = floor(known time of the signal bar to whole seconds) + 2 s (code/th_nyeng/ny_build.py:32; code/th_brkt/brkt_build.py:42); events with ts >= the session-end instant are dropped (ny_build.py:33, brkt_build.py:46); session-end instant = the next ET session boundary after the signal bar (code/th_swap/common.py:32-40; for NY AM = 12:00 ET); the exit cap (N = 120 s, code/th_fakefill/cap_exit.py:9,20) is applied to the event file. Only bars with session code 3 (ET 09:30-12:00; code/th_swap/common.py:41-44) and `part` = 0 (not the truncated last bar of a session) can signal (ny_build.py:29; brkt_build.py:38-39). Sample-day checks: my re-run of the engine module on the stored bars gives the engine events file exactly for both sample days (counts below) and over the whole history (counts below).
**One-position / fill / exits (SPEC text copied from autopilot/D8_BUILD_SPEC.md block (b2), simulator code/replica/sim.py: NOT re-verified here).** MARKET order sent at event time; filled 1.0 s later (LAT_FILL) walking the 10-level book (buy at the ask side, sell at the bid side); stop = stop order at fill -/+ stop_pts (triggered by a print at/through the level, then market order walking the book), target = resting limit at fill +/- tgt_pts; ONE position per book: an event while the book is in a trade, an exit is pending or an entry is in flight is dropped (the next event after the exit is traded); scheduled session-end exit at 12:00 ET + 1.0 s (if no print follows within 120 s the exit is the last print before it); contract roll: flat 1 ns before the roll second, entries skipped roll-120 s to roll+300 s. Sizes: 1 lot per book in the engine runs (bare R0 base set; no stack rules in the TRADES blocks).
